subject_definitions
<Subject 1> is the person in <Picture 1>. Use the image as the sole character reference, preserving the visible identity, hairstyle, clothing, and accessories without redesign.

summary
[reference generation] A ten-second, restrained period-drama scene beside a window and a warm lamp. <Subject 1> finishes reading a letter, folds it, and starts offering it to an unseen person. When she looks up, her expectation turns to hesitation. She quietly draws the letter back before anyone takes it.

retention_analysis
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved from <Picture 1> across all shots.
<Picture 1> defines the character and visible wardrobe, not a mandatory first frame, pose, background, or layout. Do not reproduce its watermark or signature.
Introduce one paper letter, one wooden table, and one shaded warm lamp as new scene props. The intended recipient stays entirely off-screen.

detailed_description
Photorealistic cinematic imagery in a quiet traditional room at dusk, with soft cool window light balanced by a steady warm lamp. Use vertical 3:4 framing, natural skin texture, clearly visible eyes, and shallow background separation; preserve the delicacy of the reference without magical effects.

[Shot 1] Begin with a seated, eye-level three-quarter medium close-up of <Subject 1> beside a wooden table. Frame her head, upper body, and hands together. The window lies to one side, while a single shaded lamp sits farther back on the table, outside her hand movements. Its warmth complements the broad window light rather than casting her face into darkness. The table is otherwise uncluttered.

During the first two seconds, she holds one small paper letter in both hands just below chest height and finishes reading its final lines. Her gaze tracks downward once, then pauses; a faint expectation softens her mouth. Keep the written side toward her so no readable text needs to appear. The letter stays below her face and does not hide her eyes or mouth.

Between two and four seconds, she folds the letter once along an existing central crease. Her left hand steadies the lower half, and her right hand closes the fold. She then holds the folded letter between her right fingers, with her left fingertips lightly supporting its lower edge, and extends it a short distance toward the unseen recipient beside the camera. Her eyes begin to lift. Keep the entire gesture gentle and purposeful, with anatomically natural hands and no extra paper or envelope.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, cut to a facial close-up on the same side of the eyeline. She meets the unseen person's gaze just beside the lens. For a brief moment she waits, still expecting a response. No response arrives. Her eyes search subtly, the suggestion of a smile fades, and her lips part slightly before closing again. She does not cry or suddenly look angry. Her hands remain extended below the crop, still holding the same folded letter. The camera stays nearly still, allowing the change from hope to restraint to become readable.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut back to the original medium close-up, preserving the extended letter and hand positions. She lowers her gaze first, then deliberately draws both hands back toward herself. The other person never touches the letter. She brings it to rest in her hands just above the table edge, places her left fingertips over the fold, and releases one quiet breath. End with the letter still held close and her expression composed but unresolved. Use only a minimal, slow forward camera movement over this final shot; all performance remains at normal real-time speed.

Preserve character identity, paper size, single fold, lamp position, and lighting across cuts. No dialogue, extra people or hands, handover, tearing or burning the letter, dramatic sobbing, forced smile, slow motion, freeze frame, subtitles, logos, or watermark.

overall_soundscape
Quiet room ambience, a faint breeze beyond the window, delicate paper rustling during the single fold, and one restrained exhale as she withdraws the letter. The pause after she looks up remains unanswered. No intelligible speech.

widgets_values:
subject_definitions
<Subject 1> is the person defined by the character sheet in <Picture 1>. Use that sheet as the sole character reference, preserving identity, hairstyle, wardrobe, and accessories without redesign.

summary
[reference generation] A ten-second cinematic facial close-up as a film ends. <Subject 1> holds back tears in the screen light. As the auditorium lights rise, she blinks, gathers herself, and turns toward an off-screen friend with a small, not-quite-steady smile that does not fully conceal her emotion.

retention_analysis
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved from <Picture 1> throughout [Shot 1].
<Picture 1> defines the character only, not the first frame, expression, pose, environment, or layout. Render one person; do not reproduce panels, repeated figures, labels, or reference backgrounds.
The friend remains entirely off-screen and requires no additional character reference.

detailed_description
Photorealistic cinematic portraiture with natural skin texture, shallow depth of field, and clearly readable eyes. Use vertical 3:4 composition and a motivated transition from soft screen light to warm auditorium lighting, preserving facial detail throughout.

[Shot 1] One continuous ten-second shot at normal real-time speed. <Subject 1> sits in a cinema seat, framed tightly from the top of her head to the base of her neck. Keep her entire face visible, with comfortable headroom and only a little surrounding space. A softly blurred seat back and a few indistinct background lights establish the auditorium. Do not show the screen, its content, the friend, or other audience members. Place the camera at her seated eye level, slightly off frontal, keeping both eyes visible.

During the opening three seconds, soft, pale screen light illuminates her face evenly. She watches the unseen screen with glossy eyes and a restrained, caught breath. A thin line of moisture gathers along the lower eyelids, but no tear runs down her cheeks. Her lips press together gently as she tries to contain the feeling. Avoid exaggerated trembling, distorted expressions, or sobbing. Let the tension come from how hard she is trying to remain composed.

Between three and five seconds, the warm house lights gradually rise. Their illumination softly joins and then becomes more prominent than the cooler screen light, without a blackout, sudden exposure jump, or flashing colors. Becoming aware that her expression can now be seen, she briefly lowers her gaze and makes two small, natural blinks. Her jaw releases slightly, and she quietly breathes out. She does not wipe her eyes or cover her face.

Between five and seven seconds, a faint movement from the adjacent seat draws her attention to her off-screen friend. Her eyes shift first toward a fixed point just beside the lens, followed by a small head turn. Keep the angle modest so both eyes remain readable. Her lips part as if she might explain, then gently close without speaking. Maintain the continuity of moisture at her eyes; it does not suddenly vanish.

During the final three seconds, she offers the friend a small closed-mouth smile. One corner of her mouth lifts tentatively before the smile settles, while her eyes remain visibly affected. This is an effort to reassure the friend, not a sudden change to cheerful laughter. Hold that fragile contrast: the smile says she is all right, while the eyes still carry the feeling. Use only a very slow forward camera movement of a few centimeters over the shot, maintaining sharp eye focus. End with natural breathing and a tiny residual movement at her mouth, not a frozen pose.

Keep the character consistent through the lighting change. No cuts, slow motion, falling tears, broad laughter, readable text, subtitles, logos, flashbacks, or extra people.

overall_soundscape
A faint final tonal decay from the cinema speakers fades into quiet auditorium ventilation. Near five seconds, a soft seat creak and slight clothing rustle come from the off-screen friend. One restrained exhale and quiet natural breathing remain audible. No intelligible dialogue or sobbing.

widgets_values:
尺寸对应总像素（不然会崩）
数值越大，总像素越高，画面理论细节越多，但不等于视频质量越好，H3 有上限坑。
2.0（1920×1088）分辨率最高
❌但不要直接开 2.0，对 Minimax H3 属高危档位
分档位解读
0.2‑0.4 mp
低分辨率，画面模糊，细节少；适合快速预览测试。
✅0.5‑0.7 mp【黄金稳定区间】（最推荐日常出片）
16:9 →960×544 ~1152×640
细节足够，闪烁少、肢体崩坏概率低，人物不容易变形。
0.8‑1.0 mp 高像素档位
分辨率更高，细节会多一点，但副作用明显：更容易画面闪烁、肢体崩坏、人脸漂移；
1.2 ~2.0 mp（1920×1088）高危档位
像素最高：H3 模型原生训练并没有大量 1080P 样本；
开 2.0 经常出现：疯狂闪烁、肢体错乱、物体抖动，很多时候反而画质观感不如 0.6‑0.7；

| 0.3 | 16:9 | 736 x 416 |

| 1.8 | 16:9 | 1824 x 1024 |
| 2.0 | 16:9 | 1920 x 1088 |
